summary: A clearly Chinese title and abstract overrides an OpenAlex "en" language report at evaluation time (source 'chinese_text_over_metadata'), so Chinese projects no longer lose real Chinese papers that OpenAlex mislabelled; an English-only project still excludes them (language_not_allowed).
scope_note: Worktree zh-title-language from main 9c448a3. One derivation in App._paper_language; every feed, daily-batch and creation path already reads language through it and eligibility.evaluate. Second commit (f6c49fe is the first, which changed app/service.py and tests/test_baidu_refresh.py): bilingual-title first-segment rule in app/paper_language.py; files lists this commit's paths. Third commit (independent review): strict majority-Han abstract when overriding an en report; en-only projects keep title_language_unverified for such papers; end-to-end and exact-source tests. files lists this commit's paths (the harness requires exact current paths); the first commit also changed tests/test_baidu_refresh.py.

budget_impact.rationale: A local regex check on title and abstract at evaluation time; no model call, network, new storage or data leaving the machine.
budget_impact.before: 6 real Chinese papers in a zh-only project were excluded as language_not_allowed because OpenAlex said en
budget_impact.after: such papers count as zh when the text is clearly Chinese

reviews.reviewer: Separate review agent, read-only; no blocking issue; should-fix items (loose abstract rule on the en-override path, en-only reason, HANDOFF claim about creation candidates) fixed in the third commit

open_risks: Second commit: chinese_text_language also judges the first segment of a bilingual title (separators | ⸺ —— ' - ' ' – ' ' : ' and ':' before Latin text, remainder mostly Latin); a title whose Chinese part has no such separator is still not recognised.
Not checked against the owner's real database; the evidence counts come from the coordinator's read-only copy.
